A simple standard

Four checks before a recommendation

A strong shortlist should help parents compare real trade-offs—not just repeat a product label.

1. Age fit

Instructions, size and complexity should suit the intended stage.

2. Everyday value

How often will it be used, and can it adapt as interests change?

3. Practical details

Cleaning, storage, setup and portability all affect real use.

4. Clear trade-offs

Useful guidance includes limitations as well as advantages.
